newsitem.title: NEPAL: Germany's Lufthansa abandons Nepal route.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Lufthansa abandons Nepal route.

text.p: German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG has dealt a blow to Nepal's tourism industry by deciding to stop flying to the Himalayan kingdom from next May, officials said on Thursday.
Lufthansa, the only European airline providing a direct service to Nepal, announced on Wednesday that it would terminate its thrice-weekly Frankfurt-Kathmandu flight to cut losses.
It said cumulative losses on the route increased to seven million marks last year from four million in 1994.
"Profitability on this route has actually become retrogressive," Viktor Pompe, Lufthansa's regional director for South Asia, told reporters.
Nepali tourism officials said the decision dealt a blow to the government's hopes of attracting more than half a million tourists in 1998.
"It will definitely affect the target of achieving the goal of 500,000 tourists (a year)," Rabi Poudel, vice-president of Nepal Association of Travel Agents (NATA), told Reuters.
Last year the Himalayan kingdom, home to 11 of the world's 14 highest mountain peaks, earned $116 million from 363,000 tourists. Of them, 30,000 were Germans.
Nepali tour operators said the goal was modest considering recent double-digit tourism growth in the country.

But Royal Nepal Airlines, which also flies to Europe, cannot be counted on singlehandedly to handle the increased number of tourists which the government wants to attract, Tourism Ministry officials said.
Tourism is a major source of foreign exchange earnings for Nepal, one of the 10 poorest countries in the world.
Officials predicted the move by the German carrier would have a strong psychological impact.
"We have to look at alternative arrangements to fill in the gap," said Dipendra Purush Dhakal, a senior official in the Ministry of Tourism and Civil Aviation.
Dhakal said the government would liberalise its air policy and allow private airlines to operate on international routes.
